about: Spec 1 W9a (I-17): the one fold table. The SQL functions private.normalize_for_filter and private.match_form (migration 16) and supabase/functions/_shared/unicode_normaliser.ts are written from it; opinion_filter_contracts.sql and unicode_normaliser.test.ts check every entry. Change a rule here, in the migration that re-creates the two SQL functions, and in the goldens, together. Base form: base.compat_pins folded, NFKC, simple lower case, base.remove dropped, base.confusables and base.digits folded, base.separators to a space, NFC (a removed character can part a letter from its mark), spaces collapsed and trimmed. Match form: match.between_ascii_letters folded (! and | with an ASCII letter on both sides become i and l), then the base form, match.west_african folded, NFD, match.strip_marks dropped, NFC, base.confusables again (a look-alike that carried a mark), match.leet folded, match.separators to a space, spaces collapsed and trimmed. The match form is idempotent (a stored term is its own match form): match.separators holds < = > because NFD turns U+2260, U+226E and U+226F into them plus U+0338. Both forms are match keys, never stored for display or shown: unlike W1's display-name set, which keeps U+200C ZWNJ and U+200D ZWJ, base.remove drops both, so a ZWJ emoji sequence falls apart into its parts. match.strip_marks is the combining diacritical mark blocks (U+0300-036F, U+1AB0-1AFF, U+1DC0-1DFF, U+20D0-20FF, U+FE20-FE2F) the Cyrillic combining and enclosing marks U+0483-0489, the Hebrew points (Mn in U+0591-05C7) and the Arabic harakat U+064B-065F and U+0670 only, not every Mn character, so Indic vowel signs and viramas are kept; base.remove and match.strip_marks list whole ranges, unassigned code points included. base.separators lists no character that NFKC rewrites (U+00A0, U+2000-200A, U+2024-2026 and the like become a space or a kept character before the separator step). U+2800 BRAILLE PATTERN BLANK is a separator, not removed: it shows as a space. Unicode versions: PostgreSQL 17 normalize and lower use Unicode 15.1, Deno 2.8 (V8 ICU) Unicode 16. base.compat_pins maps, before NFKC, every character whose fold differs between the two (the Unicode 16 outlined letters and digits, Garay capitals, U+1C89, U+A7CB, U+A7CC, U+A7DA, U+A7DC and the two Todhri letters with a dot), so both ports give the same output for every code point; base.remove also drops every noncharacter. The goldens' parity entry pins a sha256 of both forms of x<c>x for every code point in its ranges: unicode_normaliser.test.ts and opinion_filter_parity_contracts.sql must both reproduce it, so an ICU or PostgreSQL Unicode upgrade that moves any fold fails a test. base.digits holds every Nd digit (Unicode 16) that NFKC leaves alone. base.remove holds every Default_Ignorable_Code_Point, assigned or not (U+FFF0-FFF8 and the whole of U+E0000-E0FFF included: text shapers hide them), and the interlinear annotation controls U+FFF9-FFFB.
